question: What is the main goal of secondary prevention in gut health?

options.A: Eliminating all bacteria from the gut
options.B: Preventing initial exposure to food toxins
options.C: Replacing lost fluids via intravenous lines

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on finding and treating health issues early before they develop into severe symptoms. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why is the mucosal barrier important for the digestive system?

options.A: It makes all essential amino acids
options.B: It speeds up the movement of solid waste
options.C: It protects the gut wall from self-digestion and germs
options.D: It prevents water from entering the bloodstream

explanation: The mucosal lining creates a defense shield that protects deeper tissue layers from harsh digestive juices and harmful microbes. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h1)

question: Which type of dietary fiber adds bulk to stool and helps waste move faster?
explanation: Insoluble fiber does not dissolve in water. It creates bulk, which helps waste move quickly and easily through the colon. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h2)

question: A patient asks why eating lots of sugary, processed foods harms the gut. The best explanation is that these foods...

options.A: destroy all enzymes made in the pancreas
options.B: block water absorption in the small intestine
options.C: cause the stomach lining to physically shrink
options.D: feed harmful bacteria and cause gut inflammation

explanation: Refined sugars feed bad bacteria in the gut, which upsets the natural balance of the microbiome and leads to inflammation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h2)

question: What does the colon mainly do when a patient is low on water?

options.A: It secretes extra mucus to lubricate the intestines
options.B: It stops moving completely to save body fluids
options.C: It pulls extra water from waste, leading to hard stool
options.D: It increases the production of digestive enzymes

explanation: When the body is dehydrated, the large intestine absorbs more moisture out of stool, which causes hard stools and constipation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h3)

question: A patient on bed rest is at risk for constipation. Which nursing action best helps prevent this?

options.A: Telling the patient to hold bowel movements until they can walk
options.B: Encouraging regular fluids and helping with gentle movement exercises
options.C: Giving a daily high-dose enema without asking the doctor
options.D: Restricting fluids so they need the bedpan less often

explanation: Drinking enough water softens stool, and movement exercises help stimulate bowel activity in patients who must stay in bed. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h3)

question: Why should you use separate cutting boards for raw meat and vegetables?

options.A: To keep the kitchen looking neat
options.B: To keep vegetable juice from staining the meat
options.D: To stop germs from spreading between foods

explanation: Using separate boards prevents bacteria from raw meat from contaminating foods that you eat raw or lightly cooked. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the most effective way to make drinking water safe from germs in rural communities?

options.A: Adding food coloring to local wells
options.C: Storing water in open clay pots in the sun
options.D: Boiling drinking water before using it

explanation: The heat from boiling kills harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites found in untreated water sources. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h4)

question: How does cigarette smoking contribute to heartburn and acid reflux?

options.A: It increases the amount of alkaline saliva
options.B: It paralyzes the muscles of the small intestine
options.C: It thickens the protective lining of the stomach
options.D: It relaxes the valve at the top of the stomach

explanation: Nicotine weakens the lower esophageal sphincter, making it easier for stomach acid to flow backward into the esophagus. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why can ongoing emotional stress trigger flare-ups of irritable bowel syndrome?

options.A: Stress hormones turn directly into digestive enzymes
options.B: Mental tension physically squeezes the large intestine from the outside
options.C: Anxiety stops the stomach from making acid right away
options.D: The brain and the gut communicate, affecting how the intestines move

explanation: The gut-brain axis connects emotional stress directly to changes in bowel movement and sensitivity through nerve pathways. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of getting a routine screening colonoscopy?

options.C: Finding and removing growths that could become cancer
options.D: Replacing the need to eat fiber

explanation: A colonoscopy lets doctors see inside the bowel and remove abnormal growths, called polyps, before they turn into cancer. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h6)

question: A patient with a family history of bowel cancer asks why their screening should start early. The best response is that...

options.A: family genes increase early risk, so early checks are safer
options.B: older screening methods do not work for younger people
options.C: polyps grow slower in people with a family history
options.D: health insurance only pays for tests if relatives had cancer

explanation: Family history can mean a higher risk of developing changes at an earlier age, which makes early screening necessary. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h6)

question: A nurse is teaching a patient from a low-resource community about safe food handling. What is the best first step?

options.A: Hand out expensive imported food thermometers
options.B: Tell them to only buy imported canned foods
options.C: Check what clean water and storage the patient actually has
options.D: Give them a complex manual on industrial food safety

explanation: Health teaching must fit the patient's real living situation and available resources to be practical and helpful. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h7)

question: Which symptom means a patient needs an urgent checkup for a possible digestive problem?

options.B: Occasional gas that goes away after walking
options.C: Mild bloating after a large evening meal
options.D: Temporary loss of appetite from mild stress

explanation: Dark, tarry stools usually mean bleeding in the upper digestive tract, which requires immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h7)
